`benmore logs [app] [-n N | --lines N] [-f | --follow] [--env dev|prod]` prints the last N lines of the instance's server log as text and exits. N defaults to 200 and must be 1 to 2000 (another value is a usage error, exit 2). `-f` or `--follow` keeps the connection open and prints new lines until interrupted; an account holds at most 4 follow streams and an app instance 6, and one more answers 429. Without `app` the app the current workspace is linked to is used. Editor access.

`benmore requests <app> [--limit N] [--env dev|prod]` (MCP get_request_logs) answers `requests` (method, path, status, duration_ms, user, created_at, plus error and request_id when recorded) and `count`. `--limit` defaults to 200 and is capped at 1000. A viewer gets end-user identifiers redacted.

`benmore decode <app> <bundle> <line> <column> [--env dev|prod]` (MCP decode_stack) maps a position in a served script back to its source: `<bundle>` is the script's file name under static/, line and column are 1-based. It answers `source`, `line`, `column` and `symbol`, or a `hint` when no source map is available (see symbolication).
`benmore health <app> [--env dev|prod]` (MCP get_health) answers a snapshot of the instance's database: `tables`, `row_counts` per table, `active_sessions`, `audit_last_24h` and `checked_at`.

`benmore activity` (MCP get_recent_activity) answers the 50 most recent platform events (`app`, `event`, `message`, `level`, `created_at`) of every app the account owns or collaborates on, dev and prod instances together.
